text:
Marathon's stock jumped 2.5% today, extending a sharp three-day rally that has pushed it up roughly $35 since early last week. The move follows comments from Trump suggesting an Iran conflict could end "fairly soon" and statements that Iran's military position has deteriorated—comments that have reduced immediate geopolitical risk to oil supplies. Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on those same hopes, but U.S. crude has held steadier around $89.62, and refineries are running at 95.2% capacity with healthy fuel inventories, keeping the outlook favorable for refining margins.

The broader context matters here: while diplomatic prospects remain genuinely uncertain (Secretary of State Rubio has said negotiations are "unproductive"), any reduction in perceived geopolitical tail risk—particularly conflict that could disrupt Middle Eastern oil—tends to support energy stocks. The recent midterm election results also signaled a voter rebuke of the Trump administration, which could complicate policy certainty going forward, but that broader political headwind has not offset the near-term relief trade in energy as war premium pressures ease.
